text:
Maria (PM): Quick sync — we need to synthesize customer asks from Q1 into a single routing/tenant isolation scope doc. who wants to own the tradeoff matrix?
Jonathan (Arch): happy to take lead on the matrix + migration constraints. will need input from SRE on operational cost.
Alex (Product): we should prioritize by: (1) SLA impact, (2) customer revenue risk, (3) implementation complexity. propose a 2-sprint spike to validate assumptions.
Sam (Eng-SRE): +1. need to quantify GPU pooling and cross-region egress cost for each option. early estimate: per-tenant slice adds ~12% infra cost for small tenants, ~5% for large.
Nisha (ProdOps): also surface monitoring/alerting requirements. if we add isolation lanes we must ship per-lane dashboards and quota controls.
Maria (PM): rough goals for the doc: define candidate policies, migration paths, launch gating criteria, and customer-facing commitment levels.
Jonathan (Arch): sketch of policy decomposition:
```
Policy types:
- Region affinity (soft/hard)
- Tenant slices (dedicated pool vs shared pool w/ isolation)
- Fallback policy (graceful degrade -> cheaper model variant or region)
- Quarantine flow (rate-limit + backpressure)
```
Maria (PM): for each policy we need: owned config surface, SLO delta, expected cost delta, rollback plan, and customer opt-in path.
Alex (Product): customer asks to fold in: legal/regulatory region pinning, high-throughput enterprise tenants wanting dedicated lanes, and retail customers wanting lower-cost fallback.
Sam (Eng-SRE): concrete launch criteria proposal:
```
- Canary success: 99.5% of requests served within target latency for canary tenants for 48h
- Regression: no >5% increase in 95th token CPU usage platform-wide
- Observability: per-tenant tracing + per-route cost breakdown live in console
- Ops runbook: documented playbook + one oncall drill completed
```
Nisha (ProdOps): add compliance checklist for Private deployments: KMS integration test, audit log retention verified, internal red-team access validated.
Maria (PM): scope negotiation point — customers asking for "hard region lock" vs our preference for soft affinity with fallback. we should offer two SKUs: "Pinned" (hard lock, SLA premium) and "Affinity" (soft, cheaper).
Jonathan (Arch): implementation notes: hard lock means strict routing table entries + capacity reservation per region; affinity uses probabilistic steering + metrics-driven rebalancing. org-level config needed.
Alex (Product): timeline proposal: spike (2w) -> design doc (1w) -> canary infra + pilots (4-6w) -> general availability (Q3). adjustable by customer commitments.
Sam (Eng-SRE): blockers: cross-region KV cache replication for large context sizes and autoscaler policies that must be per-slice. need infra tickets for autoscaler rewrite.
Maria (PM): action items: Jonathan draft tradeoff matrix + migration flows by EOD Wed; Sam produce cost delta table for small/medium/large tenants by Thu; Alex assemble customer prioritization list; Nisha add compliance checklist and ops drill owner.
routing-bot: deploy-check triggered for infra-prototype. status: queued.
Jonathan (Arch): tagging folks for design review: @Sam @Nisha @Alex — will drop a short doc in #architecture/designs tomorrow. please comment inline once available.
Alex (Product): decision question for execs: do we require billing changes (new SKU for pinned lanes) at GA? my recommendation: yes, to avoid cross-subsidy.
Nisha (ProdOps): ops concern: SKU+billing means new entitlement checks in control plane. we should scope that as post-canary work if pilot customers can accept manual gating.
Maria (PM): ok — we'll surface the billing decision as a gating item for product council next Tue. I'll draft the board slide. :spiral_calendar:
Sam (Eng-SRE): noted. I'll try to prototype the per-slice autoscaler in the spike and flag major unknowns.
Jonathan (Arch): one last risk: model compatibility across regions/variants. fallback to quantized model could be cheaper but may impact hallucination profile. add a prompt/eval run for each fallback path.
Alex (Product): perfect — add quality guardrails to launch checklist.
Maria (PM): thanks all. meeting in #architecture on Thursday 10a to review draft. if anyone wants to own the migration playbook, call it out here.
Sam (Eng-SRE): I'll co-own the migration playbook with Jonathan.
Nisha (ProdOps): I'll own the ops drill and compliance verification.
Maria (PM): great — closing thread. I'll post the doc link once Jonathan uploads. :white_check_mark:
